notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the PythonObjectDriver helper, but the confirmed entry is the function module hardware/stage.py, so this package is a direct Driver over pyfile:WIL_Pycro_Control_App/hardware/stage.py#* with a hardware wrapper in native.py. The package integrates the stage device; NOT COVERED: camera image capture. hardware/camera.py only starts Micro-Manager sequence acquisition and waits for the circular buffer; image retrieval is utils.pycro.pop_next_image, which is not an entry symbol, so the camera and its MAX_EXPOSURE/MIN_EXPOSURE limits are not bound. The e-stop calls reset_stage, the only stop-like native function: it sends the ASI RESET command, whose documented effect is clearing flash memory, the origin and joystick settings, and it first waits for the XY stage to become unbusy via send_serial_command_to_stage; general_exception_handle retries twice. The clone documents no axis-halt command, so the fake's instant stop is test data, not proof that an in-flight move stops. Hardware was not run; the hardware backend needs the clone's WIL_Pycro_Control_App directory on sys.path plus a live Micro-Manager/pycromanager installation. Fake starting and post-RESET positions are placeholders. Travel ranges are operator_required; site-limits.example.json is example-only. Risk R1 follows the focus class; this is a motorized microscope stage, not an R2 hazard class. Evidence is fake backend contract_checked only; reviewed_by is null.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct Driver over hardware/stage.py, native.py line by line, all eight facts, the four operator_required limits (no clone text states a travel), the fake, the reset path (no @reset hook, re-enable or terminal declaration, so a reset only releases the latch) and the stop at the pin. The author's pass rested on reset_stage as the e-stop: it sends the deprecated ASI RESET, which its docstring says resets the console's flash memory, origin and joystick settings (stage.py:321-334), through send_serial_command_to_stage only after the XY stage stops being busy (stage.py:51-57), so it cannot interrupt an XY move, shifts the origin under the operator envelope and would have been re-sent by the background retry of the failed stop; the clone has no stage halt, and its own abort path sends no stage command (acquisition_class.py:182-196), as the routing evidence predicted. The reviewer made the @estop send nothing and raise SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held, rewrote safe_state and the docstring, corrected the eight facts (an inferred 'deployment property' and an X/Z-swap clause cited off its line among them) and added nine (the serial XY wait, the X/Z swap, the retry wrapper that prints to stdout, the import-time camera and PLC changes, the pycromanager construction, the logging setup and the abort path) in driver.py; the fake keeps a Z target unchanged as core.set_position does (fake.py); the e-stop cases of test_driver.py expect SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED, the latch and no RESET at the backend, with a fractional focus case added; native.py's docstring states the import's device and host effects (its code is unchanged); facts.md was synced with a review section; reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json were regenerated. The gate now fails G6 (ESTOP_FAILED, ESTOP_NO_NATIVE) and G8 SAFE-028, the expected blocked state (stable digest sha256:f0055e64bd37eadcaf3eec1f726a73830c04a1e972aa52c2c82d6a7c372788e1; G9 not run, the seven package cases pass on their own), and the author's pass and e-stop notes are superseded. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Real hardware: an ASI Tiger console XY stage and focus axis driven through a running Micro-Manager (pycromanager). Nothing in the package or the clone stops a move already sent, and the clone documents no independent physical stop; never use reset_stage as a stop (RESET resets flash memory, the origin and the joystick settings). Loading the hardware backend (the server opens it at load) sets the camera default mode and programs the PLC trigger circuit (hardware/__init__.py:5-11), writes LSConfig.cfg and logs/ into the current directory and calls logging.basicConfig; failed hardware calls print to stdout (exceptions_handle.py:41), which corrupts a stdio server; at R1 the loader starts this backend without a human reviewed_by. The per-axis writes bypass move_stage's Z/XY ordering that keeps capillaries off the objective (stage.py:200-212), so a per-axis box envelope may not prevent a collision: consider R2. The X write is a serial M Z= while the X read is the Micro-Manager XY device's X (stage.py:68-71, 225, 269); they agree only where that device's X is the Tiger Z axis. Unblocking needs a stop the clone sends and confirms; Micro-Manager's own device stop is outside the clone, never called by it, and would need the user's decision on companion-source citations. The clone has no LICENSE file. Not covered: the camera entry (camera.py), whose snap waits for an image with no bound (camera.py:127-128).

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Adversarial verification of the claude-opus-5-5 review (block) by a different model (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): the verifier agreed and found no blocker or major. The block is genuine. I re-ran collect.py --strict myself and got FAIL G6,G8, as the reviewer reported. The only stop-like function in the clone is reset_stage. It sends ASI RESET, which per its own docstring resets flash memory, origin and joystick settings, and it is marked DEPRECATED (stage.py:321-334). It goes through send_serial_command_to_stage, which first calls core.wait_for_device(XY_STAGE_NAME) (stage.py:51-57), so it cannot interrupt an XY move. The clone has no HALT command. The cited lines I spot-checked with show_refs.py (stage.py:10-14 and :68-71) say what the facts claim. NO_HARDWARE_FREE_PATH is a listed code, and PLAYBOOK.md:152 describes it as a case where no honest fake is possible. It is a reasonable fit for an actuator whose stop cannot be proven or modelled without hardware. A one-line stale-file issue remains, listed below. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it.
